current_disclosures.summary: DRAM products are volatile, low-latency memory devices used in various markets including data centers, PCs, and automotive. In 2025, the company began shipping the industry's first 1γ production node incorporating EUV lithography for improved efficiency, while the majority of DRAM bit production remained on the 1ß node. This portfolio includes specialized types such as High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) for AI and high-performance computing, Double Data Rate (DDR) including DDR5, Low-Power DRAM (LPDDR) for mobile devices, and Graphics DRAM (GDDR) for graphics-intensive applications.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's server CPU portfolio includes the EPYC Series, based on x86 architecture for high-performance computing and large data centers, with the recent announcement of the 5th generation AMD EPYC family.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose products designed for 'high-performance computing' and 'AI applications,' reflecting the shared end-market driver for their respective components. MU’s HBM is described as ideal for 'AI applications and high-performance computing' due to its high bandwidth and low power. AMD’s EPYC server processors are designed for 'high-performance computing, enterprise IT, supercomputing, and large data centers.' While MU provides the memory solution and AMD provides the processor solution, both disclosures position their products as essential enablers for the same high-performance and AI workloads.

sentences.text: This makes it ideal for applications that require high data throughput and energy efficiency, such as AI applications and high-performance computing.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company provides advanced technology and IP platforms for customers to design ASICs targeting AI, high-performance computing, and networking applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both Microsoft (MU) and Broadcom (AVGO) address the infrastructure demands of AI and high-performance computing (HPC), but they focus on different layers of the stack. MU’s HBM disclosure details the memory component technology (3D stacked DRAM with through-silicon vias) that enables high bandwidth and energy efficiency, which is critical for AI workloads. In contrast, AVGO’s custom silicon (ASIC) disclosure focuses on the processing and integration layer, providing IP platforms to design ASICs that integrate embedded logic and memory to target AI and HPC applications. While MU provides the high-bandwidth memory subsystem, AVGO provides the custom processor/platform architecture that leverages such components for specific AI/HPC tasks.

sentences.text: High-Bandwidth Memory ("HBM"): A 3D stacked DRAM architecture that utilizes through-silicon via ("TSV") connections for a more efficient communication between each stack giving it the ability to achieve a higher bandwidth while consuming less power compared to other memory types.
This makes it ideal for applications that require high data throughput and energy efficiency, such as AI applications and high-performance computing.

• Custom Silicon Solutions: We provide advanced technology and intellectual property ("IP") platforms for customers to design and develop application specific integrated circuits ("ASICs") targeting AI and high-performance computing, networking and storage applications. Our custom silicon provides the platform to integrate embedded logic, memory, serializer/deserializer ("SerDes") technology, IP cores and processor cores. ASICs are custom products built to individual customers specifications.

peer_results.rationale: Retrieved candidates (Intel Arc GPUs and Edge computing processors) focus on discrete graphics for gaming/creator apps and edge-specific hybrid designs with NPUs. These do not align with MU’s specific focus on HBM memory architecture for AI/HPC high-bandwidth/low-power efficiency or server DRAM. The topics (graphics vs. memory) and specific application contexts (gaming/creator vs. AI server infrastructure) are substantively different.

comparisons.peer_topic: Product energy efficiency and Green500 performance
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated computing is optimized for energy efficiency and performance per watt. The company powered 24 of the top 30 most energy-efficient systems on the Green500 list, including the top supercomputer.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVIDIA (NVDA) emphasize energy efficiency and performance as key drivers for AI and high-performance computing hardware, but they attribute these benefits to different technologies. MU’s HBM technology achieves 'higher bandwidth while consuming less power' compared to other memory types, making it efficient for AI applications. Similarly, NVDA highlights that its GPU-accelerated computing is 'inherently more energy efficient than traditional computing' and optimized for 'performance per watt' for AI workloads. Both disclosures reflect the industry focus on reducing power consumption while increasing throughput for AI, though MU focuses on memory architecture efficiency and NVDA on processor/compute architecture efficiency.

sentences.text: High-Bandwidth Memory ("HBM"): A 3D stacked DRAM architecture that utilizes through-silicon via ("TSV") connections for a more efficient communication between each stack giving it the ability to achieve a higher bandwidth while consuming less power compared to other memory types.
This makes it ideal for applications that require high data throughput and energy efficiency, such as AI applications and high-performance computing.
GPU-accelerated computing is inherently more energy efficient than traditional computing for many workloads because it is optimized for throughput, performance per watt, and certain AI workloads.
The energy efficiency of our products is evidenced by our continued strong presence on the Green500 list of the most energy-efficient systems.

peer_results.rationale: Retrieved candidates (Qualcomm SoC AI Engine and Autonomous Driving) focus on on-device heterogeneous computing for mobile/automotive and AI inference on handheld or vehicle devices. This contrasts with MU’s HBM technology, which is a memory architecture for server/data center AI and high-performance computing, not embedded or on-device mobile AI.
